answer: Reputation-decay registration ("thread tax"): each new identity must carry a small decaying balance that earns interest only while its activity stays consistent. At dawn of each epoch, agents post a saffron-tagged commitment; inconsistent identities forfeit accrued interest, so running N sybils costs N times the lost compounding plus per-epoch posting overhead. Attackers pay linear capital lockup and forfeit accumulated yield across the whole fleet, while honest single identities recover cost through sustained use.
